event.summary: Cancelling bulk Delete loses focus for retired-only markings
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. TLDR: when only retired container sessions are marked, cancelling their bulk Delete question leaves keyboard focus without a return target. Details: MetadataAction::applies rejects every retired row (marking.rs:102-106), so MarkedBar's order is empty (235-244), and the newly conditional wrapper at 358 omits .marked-menu-toggle. ListView renders MarkedBar instead of SortMenu while effective marks remain (view.rs:5391-5415), so .sort-title is also absent. The Cancel/Close/Escape handler consumes only the question and calls lifecycle::CANCEL_FOCUS (view.rs:4375-4379); that script selects .marked-menu-toggle then .sort-title (lifecycle.rs:264-266). Neither exists, so its optional focus call does nothing after the dialog disappears. Modal DialogHandle::close schedules only the supplied return body (modal_dialog.rs:137-149); it provides no alternate return. SPEC.md Session list says: 'Cancel, Close and Escape dismiss their current question without clearing marks.' Its ordinary cancellation destination is the toolbar menu (SPEC_impl.md GUI: Dioxus, combined confirmation paragraph), which this patch removes for this supported row class. Use a surviving toolbar control, such as .marked-delete or .marked-count, when the metadata menu is absent. Suggested bucket: other; a narrow keyboard-focus regression. Confidence: confirmed by source/contract analysis only, not executed. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. Could-be-highest: no; no loss-of-work or security route is alleged. Caveats: requires a retired session whose bulk Delete opens a confirmation (e.g. last-known live agent/tabs with confirmations enabled); no claim that a completed Delete is affected. Original lead's focus-loss consequence is retained and resolved by the source checks above.

event.summary: Retired-only bulk Delete cancellation has no rendered focus return
event.detail:
Reviewed commit: 04d85f0c98a9b635709d00b056719a0baa7fd3fc. Revision reason: caller requested actual rendered-return chain and terminal/toolbar fallbacks, rather than inferring user focus solely from a missing selector. Original consequence retained: cancelling bulk Delete with only retired rows marked leaves keyboard focus without the promised return target. Source chain: MetadataAction::applies rejects retired rows (marking.rs:102-106); order at 234-243 is empty; the changed conditional at 358 removes the metadata toggle. MarkedBar still renders .marked-delete, .marked-clear and tabindex=-1 .marked-count (337-397), but CANCEL_FOCUS references none of them: lifecycle.rs:264 selects only .marked-menu-toggle then .sort-title. ListView renders SortMenu only in the else branch when effective_marks is empty (view.rs:5391-5416), while cancellation takes only the confirmation token and preserves marks (4375-4379). Thus neither selected return node exists. Cancel, Close and Escape all enter that same on_cancel (lifecycle.rs:310-335, 374-376).

Fallback checks: DialogHandle::close releases modal isolation and schedules exactly that return body (modal_dialog.rs:137-149). Its missing-target behavior is explicitly a no-op. modal_isolation.rs:212-223 removes inert/listener state without restoring a saved opener; its DOM-removal observer only releases. ScrollRegion's recovery at modal_dialog.rs:577-582 requires both region and dialog connected/usable, and its observer disposes on removal at 644-646; it cannot hand focus to the toolbar after unmount. DialogFocus::remembered stores the last control inside the modal (794-809), not an opener-restoration policy. A surviving .marked-delete is therefore available but never selected by this cancellation chain. Explicit terminal.focusSelected is a separate invoked method (assets/terminal.js:3001-3012); no call occurs from this cancellation. For the particularly clear premise of selecting the retired session itself, keep_terminal_surface rejects retirement (session_view.rs:3724 onward; test at 4325-4327), and the view draws a nonfocusable status-only retired card at 2850. There is no terminal to receive a hypothetical home-focus handoff. This does not require the selected session or row to disappear: cancelling removes the modal only. If independent user navigation or unrelated asynchronous work supplies focus, the eventual active element can differ; the finding is the missing deterministic return under otherwise stable state, not a universal claim about every concurrent UI state.

Shipped trigger premise remains explicit: the retired-only marking must include a row whose last-known agent is not ended or has tabs, with confirmations enabled, so ordinary bulk Delete asks. DeleteTarget::needs_confirmation uses those visible facts (shared.rs:44-60); retirement identifies stored launch intent without normalizing those facts, and the new ticker exclusion preserves retired tabs for whole-session cleanup (service/ticker.rs:2098-2100, 2167-2169). No claim that a terminal exists for that retired row or that all retired rows necessarily ask. SPEC.md Keyboard focus: 'Closing something the user opened returns focus to where it was before it opened, on every platform'; Session list preserves marks on cancellation. SPEC_impl.md's existing combined-confirmation cancellation target is the enabled toolbar menu, whose new absence is the regression. Fix can choose a surviving .marked-delete or .marked-count fallback. Suggested bucket: other, narrow keyboard-navigation impact. Could-be-highest: no. Confidence: confirmed source/contract mechanism under the named reachable state; physical post-close activeElement not observed because no execution/reproduction was requested. proposed_drop: false. possible_cover: none. The earlier unqualified wording is narrowed to this stable rendered-state premise, without dropping or lowering any loss-of-work allegation (none was made).
